1	# INC-20 — Crash-orphaned undertaken work: no per-task commit/push, no four-state updates, while KStore hooks held the only record
2	
3	**Date**: 2026-11-01 (small hours; North-American DST fell back that night —
4	clock-time ordering is misleading, UTC is given)
5	**Project**: Natally (`~/Desktop/DevProjects/natally-ai-studio`), R12
6	landing-replica round
7	**Severity**: Workflow-discipline / publication gap — an OS-level crash
8	(GNOME restart) killed the orchestrator session mid-dispatch. Two coder
9	tasks' edits survived only as uncommitted working-tree changes; the round's
10	CHECKLIST four-state statuses were never updated; nothing was committed or
11	pushed. Recovery required the operator to hand-direct a three-way
12	reconciliation (git ↔ CHECKLIST ↔ KStore ↔ CodeGraph) that disciplined
13	execution would have made unnecessary.
14	
15	## Summary — observed timeline (UTC)
16	
17	- 05:40Z — operator exports the planning conversation to the repo root
18	  (`2026-11-01-014013-…-repair-landing-page.txt`).
19	- 06:00–06:01Z — R12 architecture and four-state coder tasklist written
20	  (`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHECKLIST.md`; backups
21	  `*.bak.20261101_015555` beside originals).
22	- 06:03–06:04Z — round-state memory written; second conversation exported
23	  (`2026-11-01-010338-…-architected-and-checklist-ready-to-be-assigned-to-subagent-coders.txt`).
24	- Commits `e9522ff2` (architecture freeze), `df046b1b` (tasklist publish),
25	  `6c5b886c` (editorial cleanup) pushed to origin/master and
26	  remote-verified. Dispatch explicitly **HELD** for operator signoff.
27	- 06:15Z — `src/marketing.tsx` (R12-A scope) and
28	  `src/components/Astrolabe3D.tsx` (R12-B scope) edited by the next session:
29	  partial implementations of the frozen contracts.
30	- 06:19:45Z — KStore captures two parallel coder `session_meta` streams —
31	  dispatch had begun. CHECKLIST still read `assigned [ ]` and the round-level
32	  dispatch row still read NOT_STARTED/HOLD. No commit, no push, no marker
33	  flips.
34	- 08:10:34Z — last KStore hook event from that session (SessionEnd,
35	  session `d3fbc787-…`). Latest KStore review verdict remains 2026-10-28 —
36	  the crashed turns never reached a Stop review.
37	- ~08:12Z — GNOME restart; session context lost.
38	
39	## The reconciliation the operator had to direct
40	
41	| Authority | What it said | Agrees with |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| git (last commit `6c5b886c`) | Tasklist published; dispatch held; nothing assigned | CHECKLIST |
44	| CHECKLIST.md (committed = disk) | Same — all five tasks `assigned [ ]`, dispatch NOT_STARTED | git |
45	| Working tree / CodeGraph | Partial R12-A and partial R12-B already implemented, uncommitted; R12-C/D/E absent | KStore |
46	| KStore (hook captures) | Two coder sessions dispatched 06:19:45Z; activity continuing to 08:10:34Z | Working tree |
47	
48	Two consistent pairs, contradicting each other. The durable publication
49	surfaces (git + CHECKLIST) told one story; the passive capture fabric
50	(KStore) and the filesystem told the truth. Recovery was possible only
51	because (a) KStore hooks had captured everything as it happened, (b) the
52	operator had saved the two prior conversations to the repo root, and (c) the
53	R12 tasks were written idempotently, so the partial edits could be absorbed
54	by re-execution instead of being fatal.
55	
56	## Root cause
57	
58	Execution was undertaken without simultaneously maintaining the durable
59	state surfaces. Publication was treated as a task-completion-only event, so
60	all in-flight state — the dispatch itself, the assignment markers, the
61	partial edits — lived nowhere durable. The crash converted a discipline gap
62	into an incident: anything not committed, not checklisted, and not hooked
63	into KStore simply vanished; what remained had to be reconstructed by
64	forensics the operator had to supervise line by line.
65	
66	## Lesson — the three fastidious habits (canonical)
67	
68	1. **Commit and push every completed task immediately, and verify the
69	   remote.** A local commit or a deployed artifact is not publication. Never
70	   let a round's authorization, dispatch, or partial reviewed progress sit
71	   uncommitted — "the task isn't finished yet" is when the crash clock is
72	   running.
73	2. **Hooks send everything to KStore as you go — never bypass, never
74	   disable.** KStore was the only continuity channel that survived this
75	   crash intact. It is the single source of truth for "what was your last
76	   line": if you ask it, and your hooks are in order, it answers.
77	3. **Update the CHECKLIST four-state status fastidiously as you go.**
78	   Assignment `[/]`, undertaking, completion `[X]`, validation `✅` each
79	   flip at the moment they happen, so that at every instant git, CHECKLIST,
80	   and KStore agree. If you are compliant, all three match where you left
81	   off; if they do not match, the drift itself is the finding.
82	
83	## Why this binds globally
84	
85	Any session on any project can be killed by an OS crash, power loss, or
86	harness failure at any moment. The three habits are the only difference
87	between "resume from the durable record" and "archaeology under operator
88	supervision." They cost seconds per event; this incident cost a supervised
89	forensic reconstruction and risked silent loss of undertaken work.
90	
91	## Cross-references
92	
93	- Standing instruction in the project `CLAUDE.md` (commit and push every
94	  completed task; verify the remote; report publication gaps honestly).
95	- INC-3 (window-replacement orphan) — same crash-class, earlier substrate;
96	  INC-20 extends it from "orchestrator continuity" to "per-task publication
97	  + four-state + hook-capture discipline."
98	- INC-7 (proxy attestation / marker progression) — the four-state marker
99	  semantics this incident's checklist discipline depends on.
100	- `resumes-not-recovery-points` (git/KStore/task_ledger are the only
101	  authoritative recovery points; session resumes are not).
